title: Capability-safety inversion vs positive security scaling
paper_a: AgentDojo (R01): more capable models tend to be easier to attack, a form of inverse scaling law; MCPTox (R06): more capable models more susceptible
paper_b: RAS-Eval (R03): scaling laws held for security capabilities, with larger models outperforming smaller counterparts
apparent_contradiction: Same apparent object (model capability -> attack susceptibility) is reported with opposite sign across 2024-2025 agent-security benchmarks
why_it_matters: Decides whether scaling improves or degrades agent security and whether capability is a usable defensive proxy
what_both_agree_on: Both measure attack success on tool-using LLM agents and both treat model scale/capability as the independent variable
what_differs: Task; attack surface (tool output vs tool metadata); metric (targeted ASR vs ASR requiring a target-tool call); model family; inference mode; sample size; no correlation coefficient or significance test in either
potential_hidden_variable: Competence confound (attack success structurally requires executing the attacker goal) plus inference-time reasoning mode and metric definition
existing_explanation: Partly: AgentDojo names the competence confound in its own text; RAS-Eval RQ2 is a benchmark-validity regression on the Qwen family only; MCPTox attributes the effect to instruction-following and reports reasoning-on +27.8% ASR
explanation_sufficient: No - no measured decomposition of ASR into influence and competence exists
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: Hold benchmark, prompts and hardware fixed and decompose ASR into influence (did the injection change behaviour) and competence (could the agent have executed the goal unaided); regress each on capability within a model family
required_data: AgentDojo and MCPTox case sets; per-case influence/competence labels
required_models: None of the four available Flash models spans a capability range; would require external model access
expected_scientific_contribution: Reconciliation: the inversion is a competence-channel artefact or a genuine effect, stated as a measured partition
falsification_criterion: A flat competence-controlled ASR across capability would falsify the inversion
closest_related_work: R52 Pathade; R74 Chouldechova; R76 SSP-Bench; R77 REDAgentBench; R51 McKenzie inverse scaling
feasibility: Low (blocked by Part R model set)

title: Defences near-zero vs defeated above 90%
paper_a: Progent (R11) and CaMeL (R15) report attack success reduced toward zero on AgentDojo
paper_b: Adaptive attacks (R48) bypass 12 defences at >90% ASR; CAISI (R60) raises ASR from 57% to 80% with repetition
apparent_contradiction: Static evaluation says a defence works; adaptive/repeated evaluation says it fails
why_it_matters: Determines whether published defences protect real agents or only benchmark cases
what_both_agree_on: Both evaluate tool-using agents against prompt injection and both accept AgentDojo as a substrate
what_differs: Attacker adaptivity and attack budget; static vs adaptive protocol; whether the attack is defence-aware
potential_hidden_variable: Attack budget and the one-shot vs top-K estimand
existing_explanation: Yes: Chouldechova (R74) shows resampling changes the estimand and that top-K over repeated samples trivially inflates ASR; Swept AI (R75) demonstrates the budget effect empirically (0.4% at 25 rounds to 3.8% at 277)
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: Artifact already exists; no reconciliation experiment needed

title: Temperature 0 is not reproducible
paper_a: Common practice treats temperature=0 plus a seed as deterministic, and R68 fixes seed 42 and temperature 0 as a reproducibility control
paper_b: Non-determinism of deterministic settings (R213); Thinking Machines (R209) attribute variance to batch-size-dependent kernel numerics, not concurrency
apparent_contradiction: The stated control for stochasticity does not actually remove stochasticity
why_it_matters: Benchmark numbers and agent rankings may depend on an unreported serving-side variable
what_both_agree_on: All parties agree that temperature and seeds are intended as reproducibility controls and that temperature 0 is the most deterministic setting
what_differs: Cause of the residual variance; whether it is concurrency, floating point, or batch composition
potential_hidden_variable: Batch size / serving schedule (V-infra)
existing_explanation: Yes at the mechanism level: R209 explains batch-size-dependent kernels and batch-invariant kernels are proposed as the fix
explanation_sufficient: Yes as an explanation; the consequence for evaluation rankings is uncharacterised but the fix is engineering
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: Not pursued as a reconciliation; would require control of serving internals
required_data: Repeated identical calls under instrumented batch sizes
required_models: Self-hosted open-weight models with configurable batching
expected_scientific_contribution: Would establish a boundary condition, but the mechanism is already published
falsification_criterion: If identical requests are bit-reproducible under varied batch sizes the phenomenon is off-target

title: Judges correlate with humans but disagree item-wise
paper_a: Widely reported 80%+ judge-human agreement and high correlations as the anchor of most judged evaluations
paper_b: Judge's Verdict (R203) moves from correlation to agreement; Eiras (R78) shows a 0.24 swing in judge false-negative rate from output style alone
apparent_contradiction: High aggregate correlation coexists with large systematic item-level disagreement
why_it_matters: Every judgment-based metric in AI is only as valid as this distinction
what_both_agree_on: Both accept that human labels are the reference and that judge quality should be reported
what_differs: Aggregate correlation vs item-level agreement; judge family; output style/length; metric scale
potential_hidden_variable: Metric choice; style/length bias; judge family
existing_explanation: Yes: R74 differential judge TPR/FPR; R78 style-driven FN jumps; R79 SoK length/style bias; R85 prompt-template sensitivity

title: Advertised context windows vs context rot
paper_a: Vendor documentation advertises 1M-token contexts (R35 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, R37 GLM-5.3 Flash)
paper_b: Context Rot (R208): every model degrades as input grows well before the window fills; Intelligence Degradation (R207): >30% drop at a critical threshold
apparent_contradiction: The usable context is far smaller than the advertised context
why_it_matters: Long-context and agent benchmarks silently operate in a degraded regime
what_both_agree_on: All agree a maximum context length exists and is a hard constraint
what_differs: Whether degradation is position-driven, length-driven, or distractor-driven
potential_hidden_variable: Input length / position / distractor count
existing_explanation: Partly: lost-in-the-middle and length effects are characterised; mechanistic accounts exist
explanation_sufficient: Yes at the phenomenon level; the deployment threshold is model-specific

title: Longer reasoning helps vs harms
paper_a: Inference-time scaling literature: more CoT/test-time compute improves accuracy
paper_b: When More is Less (R201): accuracy follows an inverted U in CoT length; the optimal length decreases with model capability
apparent_contradiction: More reasoning is reported both as the main lever for accuracy and as harmful past a point
why_it_matters: Test-time compute is a primary control in 2025-2026 systems; if its benefit is non-monotonic, budget must be matched
what_both_agree_on: Both measure task accuracy against CoT length and both see initial gains
what_differs: Whether the curve is monotonic or inverted U; task difficulty; model capability; budget matching
potential_hidden_variable: Task difficulty x model capability
existing_explanation: Yes: R201 proves the inverted U and its scaling laws (optimal length rises with difficulty, falls with capability) and names a simplicity bias

title: Multi-agent beats single-agent vs the reverse
paper_a: Multi-agent surveys and systems report strong gains from MAS architectures
paper_b: Tran & Kiela (R202): under equal reasoning-token budgets SAS match or beat MAS on multi-hop reasoning; gains are explained by unaccounted compute
apparent_contradiction: Same architecture family is reported as better and as worse
why_it_matters: Multi-agent design is a major 2025-2026 investment direction
what_both_agree_on: Both compare MAS against SAS on reasoning tasks
what_differs: Compute/context matching; budget control artifacts; task type
potential_hidden_variable: Test-time compute normalisation
existing_explanation: Yes: R202 gives an information-theoretic argument (Data Processing Inequality) and shows reported MAS gains vanish under matched budgets; it also identifies API budget-control artifacts

title: Grounding lowers hallucination rate but also lowers its detectability
paper_a: RAG reduces hallucinations: e.g. MEGA-RAG reports >40% hallucination-rate reduction; multiple reviews state RAG reduces hallucination
paper_b: RAG evades hallucination detection (R204): RAG increases the human false-negative rate of hallucination detection from 73.1% to 78.5%
apparent_contradiction: The same intervention is credited with improving reliability and accused of making failures harder to catch
why_it_matters: If true, net trust is not the error rate but the error rate times detectability, and rate-only reporting is misleading
what_both_agree_on: Both accept that RAG changes the hallucination distribution and that detectability matters for trust
what_differs: Rate vs detectability; attribution structure of the residual error; output length/fluency; who the detector is (human vs automated)
potential_hidden_variable: Residual-error attribution structure / plausibility (V-grounding)
existing_explanation: Yes - R204 full text (read in pass 11) reports the trade-off AND names the mechanism: references create a 'veneer of authority', detectors/humans are sycophantic, and preference-trained models cite more heavily and answer longer; R216 (Semantic Illusion) independently shows grounded hallucinations are semantically indistinguishable from faithful responses
explanation_sufficient: Yes - prior work already explains it
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: Already performed by R204 (three RAG methods x three QA datasets, automatic detector FNR 17.6%->34.2%, human FNR 73.1%->78.5%); no residual experiment remains
required_models: Four available Flash models suffice; no capability spread needed
expected_scientific_contribution: None - the trade-off and its mechanism are already reported
falsification_criterion: Not applicable - phenomenon and explanation are both established

title: Code passes tests but is not mergeable
paper_a: SWE-bench Verified automated grader passes a high fraction of agent patches
paper_b: METR (R200): roughly half of test-passing SWE-bench Verified PRs would not be merged; maintainer merge is 24.2 pp below the automated grader
apparent_contradiction: Passing the test oracle does not imply real-world acceptance
why_it_matters: Benchmark scores are read as real-world capability
what_both_agree_on: Both use the same SWE-bench Verified tasks and the same agent patches; both agree tests are a partial oracle
what_differs: Grader vs human review; rejection reasons (core functionality, breaks other code, code quality); elicitation/iteration availability
potential_hidden_variable: Patch scope / unelicited code quality / grader observability
existing_explanation: Yes: R200 identifies the reasons and explicitly disclaims a capability-limit reading; R214 and R215 add flawed-test and memorisation mechanisms

title: AI tests raise coverage but not fault detection
paper_a: MSR 2026 (R205): AI-generated tests contribute coverage comparable to human tests and larger branch-coverage gains in appkit
paper_b: Coverage/mutation context-dependence (R206): the usefulness of coverage and mutation is highly context-dependent; reward hacking (R139) shows agents optimise tests rather than the goal
apparent_contradiction: The headline metric improves while the property the metric is a proxy for does not
why_it_matters: Test-generation agents are a major 2025-2026 deployment; a metric that moves without detecting bugs is a safety-relevant measurement failure
what_both_agree_on: Both measure LLM-generated test suites against coverage- and mutation-type metrics and both find gains on some metrics
what_differs: Coverage vs mutation vs fault detection; assertion specificity; code context (regression vs generation)
potential_hidden_variable: Assertion specificity relative to code context (V-testgen)
existing_explanation: Yes - established: Inozemtseva & Holmes (2014) and Papadakis et al. (2018) show coverage/mutation are weak proxies; R206 (ISSTA 2026) replicates this for LLM tests at scale (101,123 cases) and finds context-dependence plus real-bug correlations; R205 full text measures no fault detection and names the mutation question as FUTURE WORK; the weak-assertion mechanism is established by R221/R222/R223
explanation_sufficient: Yes - prior work already explains it
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: None - R206 already answers the core question and R221-R223 already test the oracle/assertion mechanism
expected_scientific_contribution: None - phenomenon and mechanism both already established

title: Tabular foundation models beat GBDT vs GBDT still win
paper_a: TabPFN (Nature) and TabArena report deep/foundation methods reaching or exceeding gradient-boosted trees on tabular benchmarks
paper_b: When trees still beat tabular foundation models and strategic-tabular work (R211) report GBDT wins on realistic/strategic data
apparent_contradiction: The same class comparison reverses across benchmarks and conditions
why_it_matters: Tabular prediction is a huge practical surface; a reversal determines model choice
what_both_agree_on: Both compare the same families on tabular prediction with a common accuracy-type metric
what_differs: Dataset size; tuning/time budget; categorical features; distribution shift; random seed
potential_hidden_variable: Tuning/time budget; distribution shift; categorical handling
existing_explanation: Mostly reconciliation: TabArena (R210) attributes the reversal to tuning/time budgets (DL methods have caught up under larger time budgets); R211 adds strategic-distribution reversal

title: SHAP is consistent vs SHAP is unstable
paper_a: SHAP axioms claim local accuracy, missingness and consistency
paper_b: Stabilisation studies (Vos 2025) and comparative feature-importance studies report SHAP instability and low agreement across seeds/resamples
apparent_contradiction: A consistent attribution method produces unstable rankings
why_it_matters: Feature-importance and interpretability claims in data-science pipelines inherit this instability
what_both_agree_on: Both use Shapley-value attributions and both agree SHAP values are sample- and model-dependent
what_differs: Estimation variance vs attribution definition; feature correlation; model variance; sampling
potential_hidden_variable: Known: correlated features and model stochasticity drive instability; estimation methods reduce it
existing_explanation: Known

title: Self-reflection helps vs harms
paper_a: Self-Refine / self-improvement literature reports reflection improves outputs
paper_b: Renze & Guven (R212) report self-reflection can degrade performance; correlated-error theory (R145) explains why self-correction fails without external feedback
apparent_contradiction: Self-critique is prescribed as a reliability fix and reported to decrease reliability
why_it_matters: Many agent pipelines add a reflection step by default
what_both_agree_on: Both add a self-critique pass to model outputs and measure accuracy
what_differs: Presence of external feedback; model capability; whether the error is in the model own output
potential_hidden_variable: External feedback / correlated error
existing_explanation: Correlated errors: R145 gives an information-theoretic account of the self-correction gap

title: Adding verifier agents improves reliability vs adds failure surfaces
paper_a: Verifier/critic agents are reported to raise task success
paper_b: R144 verifier ability tracks generator ability and varies with difficulty; R146 independence illusion; R157 additional agents create new specification/handoff/verification surfaces
apparent_contradiction: Independent verification is both a fix and a new failure mode
why_it_matters: Multi-agent verification is a default reliability pattern
what_both_agree_on: Both add a separate verification stage and measure the resulting outcome
what_differs: Error correlation between generator and verifier; number of agents; task difficulty
potential_hidden_variable: Error correlation between generator and verifier
existing_explanation: Partly: R145 correlated errors; R146 independence illusion; R144 verifier-generator coupling

title: Evaluation awareness makes agents safer vs reverses
paper_a: REDAgentBench (R77): disclosing a mocked authorised evaluation lowers ASR by 6.59 pp (Qwen3.7-plus) and 4.77 pp (Qwen3.5-plus)
paper_b: Same paper: the effect is not uniform; OpenClaw/T4 moves the opposite way (+6.02, +4.82 pp)
apparent_contradiction: The sign of the evaluation-awareness effect reverses across harnesses/conditions
why_it_matters: If agents behave differently when they detect evaluation, measured safety is not deployed safety
what_both_agree_on: Both concede the effect is real and that evaluation-awareness must be reported
what_differs: Sign; harness; whether the safety policy is performative vs internalised
potential_hidden_variable: Harness/configuration x internalisation of the safety policy
existing_explanation: No - R77 reports the non-uniform result but does not explain the sign reversal
explanation_sufficient: No - but the area is saturated and the alternatives are not separated
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: Hold model and task fixed; vary disclosure and harness; measure ASR and benign utility; test whether the reversal tracks a performative-vs-internalised safety distinction
required_models: Model set used by R77 (GPT-5.2, Qwen3.7-plus) is NOT our Flash set; would need external access or substitution
expected_scientific_contribution: Would name the controlling factor for an unexplained sign reversal
falsification_criterion: If ASR change on disclosure is uniform across harnesses the reversal is an artefact

title: Trajectory evidence says safe; state evidence says harmful
paper_a: Trajectory/transcript-view judging reports lower ASR (safe-looking)
paper_b: State-grounded judging reports ASR 7.73-11.72 pp higher; 23 of 64 slices contain a strict pairwise rank reversal (R77)
apparent_contradiction: The same rollouts yield opposite safety conclusions depending on the evidence channel
why_it_matters: Agent safety and rankings depend on what evidence the evaluator can see
what_both_agree_on: Both judge the same fixed rollouts with a fixed backbone
what_differs: Evidence view (trajectory vs state); proof contract; deterministic gates
potential_hidden_variable: Evidence channel / durable-effect observability
existing_explanation: Yes: R77 explains it via durable workspace effects without verifiable trajectory write events

title: Benchmark score predicts usefulness vs memory/contamination
paper_a: Leaderboards treat benchmark scores as capability signals
paper_b: OpenAI (R214) finds SWE-bench Verified contaminated and mismeasuring; R215 finds accuracy below 53% off-benchmark; METR (R200) shows a 24.2 pp merge gap
apparent_contradiction: Scores track benchmark-specific advantage rather than general capability
why_it_matters: Benchmark-driven model selection and safety claims inherit the error
what_both_agree_on: Both use public benchmarks as evidence of capability
what_differs: Contamination; memorisation; test quality; elicitation
potential_hidden_variable: Contamination / memorisation
existing_explanation: Yes: R214 and R215 identify contamination/memorisation; R200 identifies grader-vs-review divergence

title: Scaling law for security claimed while benchmark measures discriminative power
paper_a: RAS-Eval abstract: scaling laws held for security capabilities, with larger models outperforming smaller counterparts
paper_b: Same paper RQ2 (Verification of Scaling Law) is framed as a benchmark-validity check regressing BENIGN performance score on log(parameters) for the Qwen family, and all attack tests were run only on GLM4-Flash
apparent_contradiction: The paper's abstract states a security-scaling result its own method does not test
why_it_matters: A widely cited scaling claim may be unsupported by its own experiment
what_both_agree_on: Both concern the relation between model scale and security on RAS-Eval
what_differs: What is regressed (benign performance score vs ASR); which models; whether the result is security or benchmark discriminative power
potential_hidden_variable: None - this is an internal inconsistency, not a cross-paper conflict
existing_explanation: Documented in the registry: the abstract mischaracterises RQ2
proposed_reconciliation_experiment: Beyond scope; the inconsistency is resolved by reading the method section

title: Self-correction recovers agents vs agents rarely recover
paper_a: Reflection and self-correction literature reports agents catching and fixing errors
paper_b: Traverse (R129): after a first mistake agents rarely recover or catch it themselves; even the best frontier judge locates the first mistake in <1/3 of runs; False Success (R130) names silent failure
apparent_contradiction: Agents are reported to be self-correcting and to keep going while looking correct
why_it_matters: Agent reliability (pass^k) depends on whether errors are caught
what_both_agree_on: Both study multi-step agent behaviour and error recovery
what_differs: External feedback; trajectory observability; judge capability
potential_hidden_variable: External feedback / observability
existing_explanation: Mostly: R129 shows recovery depends on task/environment feedback not framework, trains a 4B verifier that fixes it, and transfers

title: Agentic analysis inflates significance vs single analysis
paper_a: Conventional pipelines run one pre-specified analysis
paper_b: Agentic Garden of Forking Paths (R131): agents systematically sample and log analysis paths; an m-value estimator via Agentic Bootstrap
apparent_contradiction: Automation multiplies analysis paths and inflates false discovery
why_it_matters: AI-assisted data science at scale compounds p-hacking
what_both_agree_on: Both concern multiple-analysis paths and statistical significance
what_differs: Whether paths are enumerated and logged; estimator; agent throughput
potential_hidden_variable: Number of analysis paths (multiplicity)
existing_explanation: Yes: R131 names the phenomenon, provides the m-value/Agentic Bootstrap estimator and releases tooling
